title: Tor amplitude of a quasi-coherent complex is tested on quasi-coherent modules
statement: Let X be a quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], let E be an object of D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category], and let a\le b be integers. If H^i(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F)=0 for all i\notin[a,b] and every quasi-coherent \mathcal O_X-module \mathcal F, then E has tor amplitude in [a,b]: H^i(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G)=0 for all i\notin[a,b] and every \mathcal O_X-module \mathcal G.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.10.6 (Tag 08EA; label lemma-tor-qc-qs), implication (2) => (1)

proof.text: Let U be affine open in X and j:U\to X its inclusion. Since X is quasi-separated, j is quasi-compact and separated, so pushforward sends every quasi-coherent O_U-module to a quasi-coherent O_X-module [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh]. Thus every quasi-coherent module on U is the restriction of a quasi-coherent module on X (take j_*G and use j^*j_*G = G for an open immersion). Restriction of derived tensor to an open [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde, part (1)] gives (E tensor^L_{O_X} j_*G)|_U = E|_U tensor^L_{O_U} G, and restriction to U is exact, so commutes with cohomology sheaves. Restricting the assumed vanishing to U therefore gives H^i(E|_U tensor^L G)=0 for every quasi-coherent G on U and i outside [a,b]. Note also that E|_U lies in D_QCoh(O_U), since restrictions of quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.10.6 (Tag 08EA), proof, paragraph beginning 'Let U subset X be an affine open'

proof.text: Write U = Spec(A). By [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence], E|_U is isomorphic to \widetilde{M^bullet} for a complex M^bullet of A-modules. For each A-module N, [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde, part (3)] gives E|_U tensor^L_{O_U} N~ = (M^bullet tensor_A^L N)~; since the associated-sheaf functor is exact and an A-module P is zero when P~ is zero, the preceding step applied to G = N~ says that H^i(M^bullet tensor_A^L N)=0 for i outside [a,b]. Hence M^bullet has Tor amplitude in [a,b]. The affine Tor-amplitude criterion [lem-pc-affine-tor-amplitude-criterion] then gives that E|_U has Tor amplitude in [a,b], that is H^i(E|_U tensor^L H)=0 for every O_U-module H and i outside [a,b].

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.10.6 (Tag 08EA), proof, final paragraph invoking Lemma 36.10.4 (Tag 08E9)

proof.text: For any O_X-module G, restriction of derived tensor to U [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde, part (1)] identifies (E tensor^L_{O_X} G)|_U with E|_U tensor^L_{O_U} G|_U. Step 2 makes the latter cohomology vanish outside [a,b] on every affine open U. Since a sheaf vanishes when all its restrictions to the opens of an affine open cover vanish, H^i(E tensor^L G)=0 for i outside [a,b]. This is the asserted Tor amplitude. (The quasi-separated hypothesis is used only in step 1.)
